newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland cuts fuel excise tax, raises price caps.
newsitem.headline: Poland cuts fuel excise tax, raises price caps.

text.p: Poland cut the excise tax on diesel fuel and raised official caps on diesel and petrol prices from October 9 until the end of the year, a finance ministry spokeswoman said on Friday.
Anna Sobocinska told Reuters the ministry cut the excise tax on imported and domestically produced diesel fuel by 60 zlotys per tonne to 400 zlotys and 360 zlotys respectively.

The ministry, which controls fuel prices, also raised the maximum diesel price by 4.9 percent to 1.28 zlotys per litre, and by 0.7 percent on 94 octane leaded and 95 octane unleaded petrol to 1.51 zlotys and 1.66 zlotys respectively.

The regulations, together with a 400,000-tonne duty-free diesel import quota, were published in a government bulletin of laws on Wednesday, but only late on Thursday did the government press office issue a statement on the new regulations.

The statement said the decisions on the fuel market, long dogged by diesel shortages due to official domestic caps on fuel prices and rising world oil prices, were made at a closed cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
No information on the meeting's agenda or outcome had been released before or after the meeting.
The statement said the recent decisions sought to compensate fuel producers and importers for price rises on international markets.
